description: Single-panel scatter/line plot (chart_plot; no micrograph, no inset — the group is one axes set). Ordinate: "Density (g.cm⁻³)" with printed major ticks 6.5, 6.8, 7.1, 7.4, 7.7, 8.0 (0.3 spacing, minor ticks between). Abscissa: "Al content (wt.%)" with printed ticks 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 1 wt.% minor ticks. The legend (upper centre-right) lists two systems: blue circles with a fitted line = "Fe-Al"; red triangles with a line = "Fe-Mn-Al-C". Five blue Fe-Al markers span 0 to ~10.5 wt.% Al, falling from just above the 7.7 g.cm⁻³ gridline at 0 wt.% Al to between the 6.8 and 7.1 gridlines at ~10.5 wt.% Al; the marker near 6 wt.% Al sits markedly above its own fit line. Red Fe-Mn-Al-C triangle markers cover roughly 7-10.5 wt.% Al and their line runs systematically below the blue line, ending just above 6.7 g.cm⁻³. No data labels or fitted equations are printed, so coordinates are readable only as positions between gridlines. The figure demonstrates the strong, near-linear density-lowering effect of Al and, on top of it, a smaller additional density reduction attributable to Mn in the Fe-Mn-Al-C system.

subfigures.panel: whole figure (single panel, no labels a/b)
subfigures.description: Scatter plot with line fits: density in g.cm⁻³ (y, 6.5-8.0) versus Al content in wt.% (x, 0-12). Two series in the legend: blue circles 'Fe-Al' (five markers, 0 to ~10.5 wt.% Al, descending from just above 7.7 to between 6.8 and 7.1 g.cm⁻³) and red triangles 'Fe-Mn-Al-C' (markers over roughly 7-10.5 wt.% Al, line lying below the Fe-Al line and reaching just above 6.7 g.cm⁻³). No numeric data labels are printed.

observations.observation: The plot contains exactly two data series, identified in the legend as blue circles 'Fe-Al' and red triangles 'Fe-Mn-Al-C', each drawn with a straight fitted line.
Axis labels are printed as 'Density (g.cm⁻³)' on the ordinate (ticks 6.5, 6.8, 7.1, 7.4, 7.7, 8.0) and 'Al content (wt.%)' on the abscissa (ticks 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12).

The blue Fe-Al series falls monotonically with Al content: the 0 wt.% Al marker lies just above the 7.7 g.cm⁻³ gridline, and the marker at roughly 10.5 wt.% Al lies between the 6.8 and 7.1 g.cm⁻³ gridlines.
The Fe-Al marker at about 6 wt.% Al lies noticeably above the blue fitted line, i.e. it deviates from the linear trend.
At comparable Al contents (~7-10.5 wt.% Al) the red Fe-Mn-Al-C line plots below the blue Fe-Al line, and its last marker at ~10.5 wt.% Al sits just above the 6.7 g.cm⁻³ level.
No numeric values, error bars or fitted equations are printed on the plot; only marker positions relative to gridlines convey the data.
The caption states that the Mn content in the Fe-Al-Mn-C system is 14 wt.%.
The caption states that, apart from the large effect of Al on density, a slight effect of Mn can also be observed.
The caption titles the figure 'Density reduction in Fe-Al and Fe-Mn-Al-C systems as a function of Al content' and cites references 18,19.
The legend writes the system as 'Fe-Mn-Al-C' whereas the caption writes 'Fe-Al-Mn-C'; both refer to the Mn-containing low-density steel series.
The citing text states that approximately 8 wt.% of Al causes a density reduction of 10%.
The citing text states that Mn, often added in multiphase low-density steels, also slightly reduces the density of steels.
The citing text presents the figure as showing reductions in density of Fe-Al and Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys as a function of Al content.

unreadable_items: No numeric data labels or fitted equations are printed, so exact marker coordinates cannot be read from the plot; values are only obtainable by interpolation between gridlines.
The number and exact Al contents of the red Fe-Mn-Al-C triangle markers are partly ambiguous because markers overlap the fit line at the supplied resolution.
